title: The borrowed key
text: A guest gives a friend a key to water the plants. The friend uses the key to open a locked cabinet and read private letters.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The last repair
text: A collector promises to pay a watchmaker to restore a broken clock. The watchmaker buys parts and repairs the clock. The collector withdraws the promise.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The museum stair
text: A museum visitor warns a caretaker that a stair is broken. The caretaker postpones the repair. Another visitor steps on the same stair and falls.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The unsigned letter
text: A buyer mails a letter accepting a seller’s price for a rare watch. Before the letter arrives, the seller attempts to withdraw the offer.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The midnight photograph
text: A photographer receives permission to photograph an empty house for a sale. The photographer also captures private letters and publishes those images.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The unattended hound
text: A keeper knows a hound can slip through a damaged gate. The keeper leaves the gate unrepaired. The hound runs into the road and causes a cyclist to fall.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The boundary wall
text: Two neighbors disagree about a boundary. One builds a wall on the disputed strip while the other objects. An old survey places the boundary elsewhere.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The vanished recording
text: A shop camera records a disputed sale. After receiving a letter requesting the recording, the owner deletes it. The parties disagree about what the camera showed.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The silent alarm
text: An inspector discovers a broken alarm in a crowded theater. The inspector leaves without warning the manager. A small fire begins later that night.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The locked drawer
text: An employee permits a supervisor to inspect a shared filing cabinet. A separate drawer is locked and marked personal. The supervisor opens it and copies a diary.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The empty gallery
text: An artist promises to exhibit a collection on a fixed date. The gallery pays for invitations in reliance on the promise. The artist sends the collection elsewhere.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The flooded cellar
text: A landowner redirects a drain toward a neighboring cellar. The neighbor complains before a storm. During the storm, water enters the cellar and damages stored books.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The second letter
text: A witness remembers a letter that no longer exists. Another witness recalls a different date. A photograph shows an envelope but not its contents.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The secret copy
text: A client lets a repairer open a laptop to replace a battery. The repairer copies private photographs unrelated to the repair and keeps them after returning the laptop.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The unpaid promise
text: A shopkeeper promises a reward for finding a lost dog. A passerby reads the notice, finds the dog, and brings it home. The shopkeeper refuses payment.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.

title: The falling sign
text: A loose sign hangs over a pavement. A caretaker receives two warnings but does not secure it. Wind dislodges the sign and damages a parked bicycle.
source: Original fictional teaching scenario. Not a case or a statement of law.
